misconception_description: Student believes that conditional statements, i.e., Python statements that evaluate to either True or False, must always be wrapped in if/else statements to be returned as Boolean values.

solutions.generated_code:
program CekTandaBerlawanan
kamus
  a, b : integer
  hasil : boolean
algoritma
  input(a, b)
  if (a < 0 and b > 0) or (a > 0 and b < 0) then
    hasil <- true
  else
    hasil <- false
  endif
  output(hasil)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student wraps the boolean expression ((x ^ y) < 0) in an if/else statement because they believe this is necessary to return a boolean value. They don't realize they could simply return the expression directly. The code still functions correctly and produces the right output, but uses an unnecessary if/else structure. From the student's perspective, this is the proper and required way to convert a conditional expression into a return value.
